exam.title: MIT 8.01: Kinematics, Newton's Laws & Energy Conservation
exam.description: Undergraduate classical mechanics exam evaluating 2D projectile motion, friction dynamics, work-kinetic energy theorem, and conservative forces.
exam.instructions: Answer all questions rigorously showing all work where applicable. Time limit: 60 minutes.

questions.text: A mass m moves in a horizontal circle of radius R with constant speed v. What is the net work done on the mass by the centripetal force during one complete revolution?
questions.rubric: The centripetal force is always perpendicular to the displacement vector (F . dr = 0), so the work done over any interval in uniform circular motion is exactly 0 J.

questions.text: For a conservative one-dimensional force with potential energy function U(x) = a * x^2 - b * x^4 (with a, b > 0), the equilibrium point at x = 0 is:
questions.rubric: dU/dx = 2ax - 4bx^3 = 0 at x=0 (equilibrium). d^2U/dx^2 = 2a - 12bx^2. At x=0, d^2U/dx^2 = 2a > 0 (concave up), indicating a local minimum and stable equilibrium.

questions.text: A block of mass M slides down an inclined plane with angle theta and kinetic friction coefficient mu_k. Using Newton's Second Law, derive the formula for the acceleration a of the block down the incline.
questions.rubric: Full marks require showing forces: parallel component F_parallel = M g sin(theta), normal force N = M g cos(theta), friction force f_k = mu_k N = mu_k M g cos(theta). Applying F_net = M a yields a = g (sin(theta) - mu_k cos(theta)).
